text.p: Pub owner Ballarat Brewing Co Ltd said on Wednesday it has recommended shareholders accept the revised A$2.65 per share offer from Foster's Brewing Group Ltd in the absence of a higher offer.
Foster's is making the bid through its Carlton and United Breweries Ltd (CUB) unit.
"...Your independent directors recommend that you accept CUB's revised offer in the absence of a higher offer," Ballarat said. Foster's already owns about 43 percent of Ballarat.
The brewing group raised its offer earlier this week from its original A$2.50 bid. The revised offer values Ballarat at A$69.36 million.
Earlier on Wednesday, Guinness Peat Group Plc, which had also made an offer of A$2.50 per Ballarat share, accepted the Foster's bid for its 17.9 percent stake.
Ballarat said the Foster's offer falls within the valuation range of A$2.56 to A$2.93 assessed by the independent expert, Grant Samuel and Associates.
"Nonetheless, your independent directors consider the revised offer price does not fully recognise the future potential of the company," Ballarat said.

It said that as a consequence of Guinness' decision, Foster's would own more than 52 percent of Ballarat Brewing, securing control and making the prospect of a higher takeover offer from a third party very remote.
"Your independent directors' intend to accept CUB's revised offer in the absence of a higher offer, for the shares they own," Ballarat said.
Ballarat shares closed three cents down at A$2.62.
